_comment:
English copy for the Ihsaanly website. Every other language is site/i18n/.json with the same shape; any key it leaves out falls back to English and is listed by `bun run build:site`. Keys named _comment or ending in _comment are notes for translators and are never shown. Values may contain only , , and
. Words in braces such as {privacy} are filled in by the build or the page: keep them exactly as written, and move them wherever the sentence needs them. Keep the product name Ihsaanly, the company name Mohd Inc. and the store names App Store and Google Play in Latin letters.

day.title: You mark the prayer. The sunnah appears.
day.intro: Tap Dhuhr when you have prayed it, and the dhikr that follows is waiting. The app shows the part of the day you are in, not a clock time, so it never competes with your mosque’s timetable.
day.maghribFirst: The day begins at Maghrib, so the app’s day does too.

timeline._comment: The day as a timeline, one row per prayer. The prayer names are usually kept as they are.
timeline.ishaWhat: Two rak’ah after, then Witr. Before you sleep, Ayat al-Kursi, the Quls and the dua for sleeping.
timeline.fajrWhat: The dua on waking, and two rak’ah before the prayer.
timeline.sunriseWhat: The morning adhkar, and Duha once the sun is up.
timeline.dhuhrWhat: Two or four rak’ah before, and two after.
timeline.asrWhat: The evening adhkar, until Maghrib comes round again.

day.outro: After every prayer, the tasbih and Ayat al-Kursi. For the moments no clock can find, such as leaving home, setting off or going up a flight of stairs, the duas are a tap away on a home screen widget.

source.title: Every item shows its source
source.intro: Each act shows where it comes from: the verse, or the hadith collection with its reference and grading, and who graded it where the collection does not carry its own. Where scholars differ, the app says so rather than choosing for you.
source.plain: Every item also explains, in plain words, why it matters and how to do it.

specimen._comment: A sample dua card. The Arabic stays Arabic; the dua titles and meanings come from the app's own translated content. Only the buttons and the source lines are here.
specimen.leavingTitle_comment: Used only if the app's content has no title in this language.
specimen.ridingGrading: Sunan Abi Dawud 2602, graded sahih by al-Albani.

coming.title: Know what is coming
coming.fasting: Fasting days appear in advance: Mondays and Thursdays, the White Days, Ashura, Arafah and the six of Shawwal. They are marked “expected”, because they are calculated rather than sighted.
coming.shift: If your community’s Hijri date differs, shift it by up to two days and everything follows.

calm.title: Calm by design
calm.reminders: Two or three reminders a day, not fifteen, and nothing during quiet hours. Dismiss anything without explaining yourself. Learn a dua and mark it as known, and the app stops reminding you about it.
calm.owed: Prayers and fasts you owe are kept as a simple count to make up, never a list of dates. You will not find:
calm.neverStreaks: Streaks, scores or leaderboards on acts of worship
calm.neverFailed: A notification telling you that you failed
calm.neverPaywall: A paywall on any religious content

inside.title: What is inside
inside.adhkar: Morning and evening adhkar, and the tasbih and Ayat al-Kursi after prayer
inside.prayers: The sunnah prayers before and after the obligatory prayers, Witr and Duha
inside.duas: Duas for leaving and coming home, entering the masjid, eating, sleeping and waking, travelling, riding, going up and coming down
inside.fasting: Fasting days, from Mondays and Thursdays to the first ten days of Dhul Hijjah
inside.text: Arabic, transliteration and translation together, with how many times to say it
inside.library: A library you can search by name or by situation, and a glossary of its terms
inside.widgets: Ten home screen widgets, from what is relevant now to the days coming up

private.title: Private by default
private.pledge: Your worship data never leaves your phone unless you choose to send it.
private.none: No account, no server, no analytics and no advertising. The app works fully offline, and fully without a single permission: decline location and choose your city instead.
private.free: Ihsaanly is free, with nothing locked. Read the privacy policy for exactly what is stored and what can leave your device.

honest.title: Honest about itself
honest.review: The content is drafted and awaiting review by a named scholar, and the app’s About screen says so. When a reviewer has approved it, they will be credited there.
honest.languages: English is the original. The app also speaks Arabic, French, Italian, Japanese, Hindi, Urdu, Somali, Mandarin and Cantonese, and those translations are drafts awaiting review by qualified speakers.
honest.languages_comment: In a translation, you may add that this page itself is also a draft translation.

questions.title: Questions
questions._comment: Each question pairs with the answer under it. 'More', 'Hijri date', 'Your data' and 'Send a diagnostic report' are screen names in the app: use the app's own wording in your language.
questions.timesQ: Why doesn’t the app show prayer times?
questions.timesA: On purpose. It tells you which part of the day you are in, and you tell it when you have prayed. A window that is three minutes out is invisible; a clock that is three minutes out contradicts your mosque.
questions.hijriQ: The Hijri date disagrees with my mosque.
questions.hijriA: Go to More, then Hijri date, and shift it by up to two days. Dates in the app are calculated, and calculation and local sighting often differ.
questions.expectedQ: Why does it say “expected” next to fasting days?
questions.expectedA: Because they are calculated, not sighted. Where readings differ, such as the ninth of Dhul Hijjah locally and the day of standing in Makkah, the app shows both rather than choosing for you.
questions.locationQ: I don’t want to share my location.
questions.locationA: You never have to. Pick your city instead, and everything works.
questions.notificationsA: Two or three a day by default, and none for the obligatory prayers unless you ask. You almost certainly have an adhan app already.
questions.brokenA: Go to More, then Your data, then Send a diagnostic report. It shows you everything it contains before anything is sent, and you choose where it goes. Or write to support@ihsaanly.app.

privacy._comment: The privacy policy. A legal text: translate faithfully rather than freely. <em> marks a path through the app's screens (shown unbroken, not italic): use the app's own screen names in your language.
privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.description: What Ihsaanly stores on your device, and the only two ways anything leaves it.
privacy.meta: Ihsaanly is published by Mohd Inc. Last updated {date}.
privacy.meta_comment: {date} is filled in by the build in this language's own date format.
privacy.summaryAccount: Ihsaanly has no account, no server and no analytics. Your prayers, your settings and your practice are recorded on your device and stay there.
privacy.summaryNothing: Nothing leaves your phone unless you choose to send it.
privacy.storedTitle: What the app stores on your device
privacy.storedMarks: Which prayers you have marked, and when
privacy.storedCompleted: Which optional acts you have completed
privacy.storedOwed: What you owe in make-up prayers
privacy.storedDay: Which items you have put on your day, and which you have marked as known
privacy.storedSuggested: Which optional act was last suggested to you, so you are not asked twice in a week
privacy.storedTravel: Whether you are travelling, and whether prayer tracking is paused
privacy.storedGender: Whether you chose Brother, Sister or preferred not to say when you set the app up. This decides only whether the app offers to pause prayer tracking, and it is used for nothing else
privacy.storedSettings: Your settings: location, calculation method, Hijri offset, reminders, language and appearance
privacy.storedHome: If you turn on leaving-home reminders, the coordinates of the one place you set as home
privacy.storedWhere: All of it lives in a database on your device. We cannot see any of it.
privacy.locationRough: Ihsaanly needs a rough location to work out the parts of the day. You can grant location access, or pick a city from a list built into the app. The app works fully either way, and it works with no permissions granted at all.
privacy.locationNever: Your coordinates are used on your device to calculate prayer windows and the Hijri date. They are never transmitted, with one exception you control: if you send a diagnostic report, a rounded version of them is in it. See below.
privacy.locationGeofence: If you turn on leaving-home reminders, the app monitors a single region around a place you set. This is off by default, uses the phone’s own geofencing, and your position is never sent anywhere.
privacy.leaveTitle: What can leave your device, and only when you choose it
privacy.leaveTwo: Two things, both from More → Your data, both through your phone’s own share sheet so you pick where they go.
privacy.leaveExport: Export my data. Your settings and your full practice record, as readable text, so you can keep it or move to a new phone.
privacy.leaveReport: Send a diagnostic report. For fixing a problem. It contains your settings, your practice record, your approximate coordinates, your device and OS version, and any recent errors. Before anything is sent you are shown a screen listing exactly what it holds, and you can read the whole report in full. Coordinates in the report are rounded to about a hundred metres. Nothing is sent until you choose to send it, and you choose where it goes.
privacy.leaveReceive: We only receive a diagnostic report if you send us one.
privacy.donationsFree: Ihsaanly is free. Every part of it is free, and stays free. There is no paid tier, nothing is locked, and there is no advertising.
privacy.donationsOptional: You may give an optional donation, which unlocks nothing and changes nothing about the app. On Android, tapping it opens your browser at donate.ihsaanly.app. That page is not part of the app, and whatever it collects is covered by its own privacy policy, not this one. We never see your payment details.
privacy.notAccount: No account, email address or phone number
privacy.notAds: No advertising, and no advertising identifier
privacy.notAnalytics: No analytics, telemetry or crash reporting
privacy.notTracking: No tracking across apps or websites
privacy.notSelling: No selling or sharing of anything, because we hold nothing to sell
privacy.siteText: This site sets no cookies, runs no analytics and loads nothing from any other company. Like any web server, the host may keep standard access logs, such as your IP address and the page requested, for security and operation.
privacy.siteStorage: If you choose a language or an appearance, your browser remembers that choice on your own device. It is never sent to us.
privacy.siteStorage_comment: New sentence (2026-09-25): the language and light/dark choices are kept in the browser's local storage.
privacy.childrenText: Ihsaanly collects nothing from anyone, of any age.
privacy.deleteText: More → Your data → Delete my data removes everything on the device and starts the app over. Deleting the app does the same, because there is nowhere else it lives.

terms.religiousGuide: The app presents recommended acts with their sources: the verse, or the hadith collection with its reference and grading.
